atoms.text: Today, the dominant form of farming in the world is called conventional farming. Other terms for it are modern farming or industrial farming. Farming has always been very labour-intensive work, but conventional farming has made it possible to farm larger areas more efficiently. This means that conventional farming has made it possible to get higher amounts of food with less work than in the past.

Conventional farming has been shaped by technological innovation. The introduction of large machines and chemical pesticides and fertilisers have made it easier to grow large amounts of food faster than before. However, there are also disadvantages to conventional farming. The downside is that it often has negative consequences for the environment. In particular, the soil can suffer from the use of chemicals and growing the same sort of crop in a large area over a longer time period.

The amount of food that is produced through organic farming is still very low in the United Kingdom. The idea of organic farming is to work together with nature to produce healthy food. Organic farmers want to return to the way farming was before industrial times and try to copy the way that plants naturally grow. That means they avoid planting only one kind of crop in the same area. They also try to exclusively use organic chemicals to protect crops from insects and diseases, instead of using harsher artificial chemicals.

They do this, for example, by planting many kinds of vegetables in the same patch and only using natural fertilisers. This helps nature to stay in balance. The soil stays healthy, the water does not become polluted and the air remains clean. However, the biggest disadvantages of organic farming are that it is more labour-intensive and, for now, often can’t produce as much food as conventional farming.
